name: Surge XT
notes: Upstream is a large JUCE synth. It needs a dedicated DSP-only setup before wadspa can expose it as a browser instrument.
blockers: The upstream build is a full JUCE application/plugin tree rather than a small LV2 DSP bundle.
A browser port needs a reduced audio-engine target plus generated LV2-style metadata/control wiring.
nextSteps: Identify the smallest Surge XT engine target that can render MIDI notes without the editor or host shell.
Generate a WADSPA wrapper that exposes a verified control subset before widening to the full parameter set.

name: Vitalium
notes: Tracked through DISTRHO-Ports for top-20 accounting, but intentionally not planned for wadspa support. A useful Vitalium port would require a browser-native wavetable editor/preset system and a major DSP/UI rewrite rather than a normal LV2-to-WebAudio port.
blockers: The instrument is centered on a visual wavetable/spectral editing workflow that wadspa does not currently implement.
A faithful browser version would need a new editable wavetable/preset asset layer, not just generated sliders over an LV2 DSP surface.
The expected porting cost is closer to a new instrument rewrite than a tractable source adaptation.

name: Odin 2
notes: Upstream supports LV2, but the JUCE/CMake build must be reduced to the DSP and metadata path for WASM.
blockers: Odin2 CMake only enables LV2 on Linux; the macOS path generates AU, VST3, and Standalone targets.
The vendored JUCE juceaide helper fails on the current macOS 15 SDK because it references CGWindowListCreateImage.
The processor is tightly coupled to JUCE ValueTree/plugin/editor scaffolding, so a real browser port needs either a JUCE-compatible audio target or a DSP-only wrapper around the Odin engine.
nextSteps: Create an Odin2 audio-only build probe that bypasses the editor and JUCE plugin formats.
Extract the generated Odin parameter list into WADSPA metadata, then validate the rendered controls with the generic slider tests.

name: Helm
notes: Built as a MIDI-controlled browser instrument using Helm's real mopo/HelmEngine DSP path, with a tested oscillator, filter, envelope, voice, distortion, delay, and reverb control surface.

name: Cardinal
notes: Cardinal is a modular host-style instrument with many bundled modules. It needs a custom reduced WASM build plan.
blockers: Cardinal is a modular host-style instrument with many modules rather than one fixed LV2 DSP surface.
A useful WADSPA port needs a constrained patch/module set and a stable browser control contract.
nextSteps: Choose a small built-in patch and module subset that can render MIDI notes headlessly.
Package that subset as the first supported Cardinal instrument before expanding module coverage.
